title: News framing of immigration
description: Participants read a news story about immigration that varied in tone (positive or negative) and in the ethnicity of the immigrant (European or Latino), then answered questions about immigration.
citation: Brader, T., Valentino, N. A., & Suhay, E. (2008). What triggers public opposition to immigration? Anxiety, group cues, and immigration threat. American Journal of Political Science, 52(4), 959-978.

human_data.source: mediation::framing, mirrored by the Rdatasets project
human_data.note: Data are fetched at run time and are not redistributed in this repository.

dvs.name: immigr
dvs.label: Attitude toward increased immigration
dvs.description: Attitude toward increased immigration (1 = most positive, 4 = most negative)

dvs.name: cong_mesg
dvs.label: Send anti-immigration message to Congress
dvs.description: Whether the participant asked to send an anti-immigration message to Congress (0 = no, 1 = yes)

dvs.name: anti_info
dvs.label: Receive anti-immigration information
dvs.description: Whether the participant wanted information from anti-immigration organizations (0 = no, 1 = yes)

excluded_variables.anx: Dropped after inspecting the human data: its string labels run opposite to the substantive direction (anxious labels correlate negatively with opposition to immigration and with the documented-direction measures), so its sign cannot be scored without a post hoc recoding. Also dropped: emo and p_harm, whose documented direction conflicts with the data in the mirrored file. This decision was made after the human data had been inspected.

declared_polarity_note: All three outcomes are coded so that higher values mean more opposition to immigration. '-1' declares them reverse-keyed relative to a favourable construct, which is what a researcher who reads the codebook would enter. Declared before the v1.3.1.2 rerun; no human outcome is used.
